verdict.rationale: PostHog's own repo describes a built-in agentic feature that turns product signals into researched reports and pull requests delivered to an in-product Inbox, and @PostHog in Slack can take tasks such as shipping a fix or answering a data question. A hands-on report confirms an in-product LLM assistant exists, but it could not create a cohort and the text input became sluggish after two prompts. The MCP and CLI items describe external agents connecting to PostHog, not a built-in assistant, so they earn no credit. Missing for 10: first-party docs for the in-app assistant's capabilities and the range of tasks it can take on, evidence it can complete write actions like creating cohorts, and positive independent corroboration of in-app task delegation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Turn signals in your product data (errors, rage clicks, failed queries, and more) into researched reports and pull requests, delivered to your Inbox for you to review and merge.
Tag @PostHog in any Slack thread to ship a fix, answer a data question, or edit content – without leaving the conversation.
A user tried PostHog's LLM integration to create a user cohort from a SQL query.
